questions.text: Huber's loss function ρ(r) = r²/2 for |r| ≤ c, and c|r| − c²/2 for |r| > c. What is the purpose of the threshold c?
options: c is the number of predictors in the model
c separates the quadratic region (normal errors) from the linear region (outlier errors), capping the influence of large residuals
c is the confidence level for hypothesis tests
c is the maximum allowed residual — observations beyond c are removed
questions.explanation: The threshold c defines 'what counts as a large residual.' Below c, the loss is quadratic (like OLS). Above c, the loss grows only linearly — large residuals are down-weighted relative to OLS, capping their influence. Observations beyond c are not removed; they are simply down-weighted in the IRLS algorithm.

questions.text: MASS::rlm() with method = 'M' removes all observations with large residuals from the dataset before fitting.
questions.explanation: rlm() does not remove observations. It down-weights them using the Huber psi-function through iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS). Observations with large residuals receive a small weight (not zero weight), so they still contribute to the fit, but their influence is capped.

questions.text: In a GAM fitted with gam(log(price) ~ s(carat) + cut), the EDF for s(carat) is 8.7. What does this mean?
options: The smooth for carat uses 8.7 observations
The carat-price relationship is estimated to be approximately as complex as an 8.7-degree polynomial — highly non-linear
The model has 8.7% of the variance explained by carat
There are 8.7 knots placed at equal intervals in carat
questions.explanation: EDF (effective degrees of freedom) measures the complexity of the estimated smooth. EDF = 1 is a straight line. EDF = 8.7 means the smooth bends approximately as often as an 8.7-degree polynomial. It does not directly equal the number of knots or observations.

questions.text: In the GAM smooth plot from plot(mod_gam), the shaded region around a smooth represents:
options: The distribution of the predictor variable
A 95% confidence band for the smooth function estimate
The range of observed values for that predictor
The residuals from the GAM fit
questions.explanation: The shaded region (produced by shade = TRUE) is a pointwise 95% confidence band for the estimated smooth function f(x). A narrow band means the smooth is precisely estimated; a wide band means high uncertainty (typically at the extremes of the predictor range where few data points exist).

questions.text: You compare lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut) and gam(log(price) ~ s(log(carat)) + cut) using AIC. The GAM has lower AIC. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The GAM has more parameters, so it always has lower AIC
The GAM's smooth for log(carat) captures non-linear structure that the linear term cannot, improving fit enough to compensate for the extra EDF
The linear model should always be preferred for interpretability
Lower AIC means the GAM overfits the training data
questions.explanation: AIC penalises complexity (+2 per effective parameter). A GAM with lower AIC means its improved fit (lower deviance) more than compensates for its extra EDF. This is only possible if genuine non-linearity exists in the data that the GAM captures and the linear model misses.

questions.text: The te(x1, x2) term in mgcv::gam() specifies a tensor product smooth that models a full 2D interaction surface between x1 and x2.
questions.explanation: te(x1, x2) constructs a tensor product spline basis for two predictors, estimating a 2D smooth surface. It is appropriate when x1 and x2 are on different scales (unlike s(x1, x2) which assumes the same scale). It models a full interaction: the effect of x1 can change with x2 in any smooth way.
